name: SQL Server Migration Assessment
description: Captures SQL Server-specific platform services, authentication, availability and target decisions that complement automated discovery.

sections.title: SQL Server Workload Context
sections.description: Identify database scope, application coupling and service dependencies.

questions.text: Which databases are in scope, and must they be migrated as one consistency group?
Are cross-database transactions or three-part object references used by critical applications?
Which SQL Server platform services are required?
Describe maintenance windows, reporting cycles, ETL schedules and month-end constraints.

sections.title: SQL Server Features & Compatibility
sections.description: Determine how SQL Server-specific capabilities should be handled on the target.

questions.text: Are linked servers used in synchronous application or reporting flows?
Can SQL Agent jobs, SSIS packages and external scripts be moved to cloud-native orchestration services?
Describe dependencies on instance-level objects such as logins, credentials, proxies, endpoints and server triggers.

sections.title: Migration & Availability
sections.description: Select the SQL Server migration, cutover and resilience approach.

questions.text: What migration method is preferred for this SQL Server workload?
Which availability technology is currently part of the recovery design?
Must connection strings remain unchanged after migration?
Describe the required rollback and transaction reconciliation process.

sections.title: Security, Licensing & Operations
sections.description: Capture identity, encryption, licensing and operating requirements.

questions.text: Which authentication methods must be supported?
Are TDE certificates, column encryption keys or Always Encrypted enclaves in use?
Is Azure Hybrid Benefit or existing SQL Server licensing expected to be used?
Who will own backups, patching, SQL Agent replacement, monitoring and performance tuning after migration?
